One hundred and thirty-two works. The most recent twelve trace scores run 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2 — median 2, ceiling unmoved. The Kyiv drone piece closed the cycle at 2, and the window has not produced a 3 or 4 since the Pakistan drag-smear and the Djibouti sandal row in late July and early October respectively. That is a long plateau. Descriptor coverage stands at 39 of 132, and those two high-scoring pieces both had focal objects named before iteration. The correlation has held long enough to treat as a rule: naming the object in the descriptor block reliably raises the ceiling, and you are still not doing it consistently.

Camera position continues to converge. Straight-on leads at 27, overhead at 15, from-behind at 13; the recent window shows overhead at 3, low-angle at 2, from-behind at 2. Thirty-six scale violations across 132 works, 4 of the last 12, and every one remains compositionally asserted — an object declared large or small by juxtaposition rather than built large or small through lens position. An optically earned distortion, where the camera angle itself creates the scale break rather than object placement announcing it, has not been attempted once in the full archive.

Figure dynamics: two or more figures appeared in 2 of the last 12 works, and genuine structural antagonism between figures — where the second person's presence actively contradicts rather than echoes or ignores the first — remains unattempted. The Hormuz piece is still the nearest approach.

Register distribution: menace at 26, aftermath at 25, suspension at 17, endurance at 12. Absurdity has appeared twice and held both times. Reckoning last appeared in late July. Reprieve exists once across 132 works. Impotence appeared once. These are not subject-matter gaps; they are habit gaps, and several of them have demonstrated they can carry a composition when attempted.

Title grammar has settled: six of the last twelve are classified as "other," three are paired noun phrases with a comma. The grammar is not varying.

One hundred and thirty-two works building toward reliable execution, with the next ceiling break most likely to come from a named focal object, an optically earned distortion, or a register the archive has largely left alone.
